value.note: ABSOLUTE pointer with no absolute device and no control loop: the kh-ramabs control object writes the commanded pixel into the guest's own pointer coordinate (guest-physical 0x0050fdac, Point{int16 x, int16 y}) and injects one 2-unit PS/2 nudge so the window server republishes it, then reads the coordinate back and re-issues on the ~5% of nudges that publish 0 px. The address is derived against ONE golden; the object verifies it at connect and refuses to write at all if it cannot. 1024x768 RGB:555/16 on Cirrus GD5446. Station QEMU /opt/qemu-rhapsody (i8259 lenient-cascade + kh-ramabs).

labctl.notes: labctl exec over a getty on COM1 (serial.sock; exec_kind serial_getty, user root, password in the gitignored <dir>/serial-exec.passwd). No network exec. Pointer is ABSOLUTE via the kh-ramabs control object on <dir>/ptr.sock: the commanded pixel is written into the guest's own pointer coordinate and published with one small PS/2 nudge. SINGLE INJECTOR - while that socket is connected nothing else may push motion or button edges at this mouse. loadvm golden.

render.stationsManifestPrelude:
# rhapsody (slot 146) — Rhapsody 5.1 Developer Release 2 for Intel (Apple, 1998):
#   the Platinum Finder on the NeXT/Mach substrate. qemu-system-i386 from
#   /opt/qemu-rhapsody (kernel-hive fork + i8259 lenient-cascade patch, without
#   which the Mach kernel loses every IDE interrupt, plus 0007 kh-ramabs). TCG,
#   pentium2, 64 MB, one 2 GB IDE disk, Cirrus GD5446 at 1024x768x16, tulip
#   (DEC 21143) bridged onto the retronet, PS/2 mouse. loadvm golden -S (the
#   daemon resumes); the checkpoint restores with OmniWeb 3.0 open on the
#   corpus web.
#   POINTER: absolute with no absolute device and no control loop — `-device
#   kh-ramabs` writes the commanded pixel into Rhapsody's OWN pointer coordinate
#   in guest RAM and publishes it with one 2-unit PS/2 nudge, so the hotspot is
#   never in the path and the device set is unchanged (no golden recapture). The
#   address is bound to the golden; kh-ramabs verifies it at connect and refuses
#   every write otherwise. Needs the station binary rebuilt with qemu-patch 0007
#   INSTALLED BEFORE this launcher.

launcherParity.reason: tracked verbatim launcher is the deployed launcher. Joined the retronet web plane 2026-08-23: the netdev went user(slirp) -> tap rhaprn0 on vmbr-rn and the NIC went i82557b -> tulip (DEC 21143), because Apple's Intel82557 driver programs the chip in flexible mode and QEMU's eepro100 model never delivers a received frame (Ipkts stuck at 0). Both the -device change and mac= bind only on a COLD boot, so the golden was re-baked cold on this device set 2026-08-23 with OmniWeb 3.0 installed; docs/lab/retronet/WEB-STATION-rhapsody.md Absolute pointer landed 2026-08-30: a `-chardev socket` plus `-device kh-ramabs` writing the guest's own pointer coordinate. kh-ramabs registers NO VMStateDescription and touches no emulated hardware, so it adds no section to the migration stream and the golden baked 2026-08-23 still restores on this device set - the pointer change needs NO recapture. It does need the station binary rebuilt with streamhost/qemu-patches/0007-kh-ramabs-guest-ram-absolute-pointer.patch, and the BINARY MUST BE INSTALLED BEFORE THE LAUNCHER (`-device kh-ramabs` is an unknown device on an older binary and QEMU refuses to start).

pointerRamAddress.note: Guest-physical address of Rhapsody DR2's own pointer coordinate, the input the kh-ramabs control object writes. UNLIKE an architectural low-memory global this is valid only for the golden it was derived against: `loadvm golden` restores RAM verbatim, so the address is fixed for the life of THAT checkpoint and no longer. RE-BAKING THE GOLDEN REQUIRES RE-DERIVING IT (recipe: docs/guests/rhapsody.md, the four-position pmemsave bias search - about an hour). A second, DERIVED copy at 0x00eae020 tracks it but is not an input; writing that one alone does nothing. kh-ramabs verifies the address at connect and refuses every write if verification fails, so a stale address degrades the station to its relative path rather than corrupting guest memory.

qemuBuild.note: Both patches verified to apply cleanly to that fork commit, in that order, and the applied tree is byte-identical to the source the branch's sandbox binary was built from. binarySha256 is deliberately ABSENT until a binary is actually installed at runtime.qemu.binary: recording a sha for an artifact nobody deployed would be a confident-looking value that was never measured. The branch's own build (/data/vms/sandbox/rhapsody-abs/qemu/prefix/bin/qemu-system-i386) hashes to a5c74522adc48194f3a59d449af408ee211433005da6e4909effaab87740a79c; QEMU builds are not bit-reproducible, so re-record from the installed file rather than reusing that.

reset.fixture: Rhapsody 5.1 DR2 with OmniWeb 3.0 open on the 1996 Space Jam corpus page (retronet gateway :80 origin, no proxy) at 1024x768 RGB:555/16 (Cirrus GD5446) — the guest home window carrying the OmniWeb.app icon behind it, bookmarks panel at the left edge, disk/home/Applications icons on the right, Trash bottom right. loadvm golden -S, the daemon resumes.

network.note: retronet web plane: a DEC 21143 "Tulip" (QEMU -device tulip) is a REAL bridged NIC on vmbr-rn via the persistent tap rhaprn0 (streamhost/stations/rhapsody/rn-tapnet.sh, called `up` from the launcher on every start), MAC RN_RHAPSODY_MAC, driven by DR2's bundled DEC21X4XNetwork as en0. NOT the i82557b the install-time Configure.app was given: QEMU's eepro100 never implements the flexible receive mode Apple's Intel82557 driver programs, so that adapter transmits and never receives (Ipkts stuck at 0). Addressed 10.99.0.22/24 with DNS 10.99.0.2 and NO default gateway - STATIC, not DHCP, because Rhapsody DR2 ships no DHCP client at all (only the BOOTP-era bpwhoami), so the reservation exists only to keep the address unique. The address lives in /etc/iftab, the resolver in NetInfo /locations/resolver, and the absent default route in /etc/hostconfig ROUTER=-NO-. Behind the fail-closed RHAPRN-IN guard chain it reaches ONLY the gateway CT 10.99.0.2, where OmniWeb 3.0 reads the corpus on :80 seamlessly (wildcard DNS, no proxy configured); never labhost, the LAN, the gallery or the internet. docs/lab/retronet/WEB-STATION-rhapsody.md
